**Yes — for `HarnessKind::Omp` only.**

**Helper:** `imported_session_id` — `crates/cw-harnesses/src/adapters/generic.rs`
- `harness == HarnessKind::Omp` → `id` used verbatim, no truncation.
- Any other harness → truncated at the 12th char (`char_indices().nth(12)` → `&id[..byte_offset]`, `unwrap_or(id)` when shorter).
- Both branches then format `format!("{}_{}", harness.as_str(), id)`.

Two OMP-reachable inputs in `import_generic_jsonl_transcript`: the filename `id_slug` (after `split_once('_')`, e.g. `2026-10-22T19-57-33-217Z_01a16530-…` → UUID part) and the `type == "session"` entry's `id`. Both pass through the OMP branch, so the full UUID survives. Note `harness` can be remapped `Pi → Omp` when the path contains `/.omp/`, which changes which branch applies.

**Regression test:** `test_import_omp_transcript` — `crates/cw-harnesses/src/lib.rs` (`mod tests`). Asserts `sess_id == "omp_01a16530-b4a1-71cb-b159-96200fb07f14"`; a 12-char truncation would have produced `omp_01a16530-b4a`, so the assertion pins the full-ID behavior.

**Uncertainty:**
- `[INFERENCE]` The assertion is satisfied by the `type: "session"` entry's `id` path; the filename-slug path is not separately asserted, so the two OMP input routes are not independently pinned.
- The non-OMP truncation branch has no assertion in the supplied source — only the OMP path is test-covered.
- The test uses `CwStore::open_in_memory()` and a temp-dir fixture; it verifies the returned session ID string, not provider-side behavior.
